ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and PCMLTFR SOR/2002-184 (FINTRAC obligations); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.31 and 83.03; Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, Part 2.1 (ss. 118.1-118.4) requiring every BC corporation to maintain a private transparency register of significant individuals; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 31; FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 as implemented through FINTRAC guidance and Canada's 2023-2025 AML/CFT amendments.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access. The BC transparency register is maintained privately by the ULC and is not part of the public corporate registry; it is accessible to FINTRAC, the Canada Revenue Agency, BC Revenue, law enforcement and designated regulators upon lawful request. Public disclosure does not apply unless the ULC acquires land, which would trigger the Land Owner Transparency Act, S.B.C. 2019, c. 23.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the passport and proof of residential address of each director, shareholder and significant individual (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in each individual's country of domicile, or a British Columbia notary once the individual is in Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention effective 2024-01-11); consular legalization required only if the source jurisdiction is not a Hague Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Status / Certificate of Good Standing / incumbency certificate for any corporate parent or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of incorporation of the parent entity (e.g., Delaware Secretary of State, Hong Kong Companies Registry, or the applicable Canadian provincial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the issuing authority, or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified bank reference letter and source-of-funds affidavit for each subscribing shareholder (AML/KYC bundle)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank of each shareholder, accompanied by a sworn affidavit of the subscriber
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank signature notarized and apostilled under the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to act as director and significant-individual acknowledgment form (UBO register annex)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each proposed director and significant individual executing in their personal capacity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the jurisdiction of signature; Hague Apostille when the document will be relied upon outside Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-closing screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, UK HMT List, and Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and Criminal Code Part II.1; PEP and close-associates (RSA) assessments under FINTRAC guidance; enhanced due diligence for any PEP or connection to a FATF high-risk jurisdiction; documented negative-hit results must be retained in the KYC file before the incorporation application is submitted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: B.C. Corporate Online - BC Registry Services, Government of British Columbia (https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca); name requests are also reachable through the federal OneStop Business Registry (https://onestop.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 and the Company Name Regulation, B.C. Reg. 251/2004, the legal name must use Latin-script English or French characters and must end with the permissible corporate designate for an unlimited liability company: 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', 'Societe a responsibilite illimitee' or 'S.R.I.'. Non-Latin scripts such as Chinese characters are not accepted in the statutory name; a parallel transliteration may be used only as an informal trade name. The proposed name must pass the NUANS search and show no confusing similarity to existing corporate names, trademarks or business identifiers.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited (misleading for an unlimited liability company unless express consent is obtained)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the administrative path is: (1) file a fresh name request (CAD 30) with curative tokens and obtain a re-scored NUANS report; (2) submit a written Request for Reconsideration to the Registrar of Companies via Corporate Online, distinguishing the proposed name from the conflicting citation; (3) preserve business continuity by immediately reserving an alternate distinctive name while pursuing the appeal; and (4) if all administrative remedies are exhausted, petition the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 238, filed promptly and in any event within 60 days of the final administrative decision. A successful reservation can be renewed for successive 56-day periods by paying the renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for this low-risk app-store business only if the ULC maintains a physical registered office and records office in British Columbia staffed during normal business hours for service of process under ss. 192 and 196 of the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57. A bare drop-box or post-office box with no human attendance is not compliant; a licensed corporate-services provider or law firm acting as registered agent is required. The records office may be co-located with the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated annual probability below 5% for a non-regulated, app-store software vendor with no physical assets in the province. Unannounced premises inspections are not a routine instrument of the BC Registrar. The likelihood rises to moderate if the ULC later acquires land, becomes a beneficial-ownership reporting entity, or enters a regulated financial activity, making the transparency register and business premises subject to audit by the CRA, FINTRAC or BC Revenue under statutory inspection powers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 10, 12, 22, 51 and 189; Unlimited Liability Company provisions applicable under BC law
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Service BC, Ministry of Finance
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Incorporation Application filed through BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow account prescribed; shares may be subscribed at nominal value, but a share subscription agreement and contribution record should be maintained
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation is duly incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) as an unlimited liability company; that the share subscription and allotment of 100 common shares to the sole subscriber are hereby approved; that the registered office is established at [street address], Vancouver, British Columbia; that the first directors, namely [name], [name], remain in office subject to section 189; that such officers as the directors may appoint in writing are authorized to execute banking documentation, open payment accounts, and make all statutory filings; and that management is directed to file all post-incorporation regulatory returns and obtain any municipal business licence required for software development operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry – Name Request service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search and request a name reservation using BC Corporate Online. Provide the proposed corporate name, alternate names, and a registered business address; the Registrar will issue a name reservation report valid for 56 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, submit three new alternatives. If the refusal is erroneous, request an administrative review of the Registrar's decision within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry via Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 – Incorporation Application, attach the executed Articles of the Unlimited Liability Company and the Notice of Registered Office, pay the prescribed fee by credit card, and submit. Upon registration, the Corporate Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for corrections, amend and refile within seven days without incurring an additional filing fee if the certificate has not been issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office of the Corporation in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is a physical location in British Columbia. Maintain the statutory records at that office, including the central securities register, register of directors, share certificates, and minutes of meetings. File any future change of address with the Corporate Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered address is non-compliant, file a change of registered office address with the Registrar and update all internal records before the next statutory filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting under the Business Corporations Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a valid first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent. Approve the share subscription and capital contribution, fix the number of shares issued, appoint initial officers, and approve execution of banking and payment account documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director's consent is absent, obtain the written consent and record a corrective minute; file an amended notice if necessary and confirm with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; BC Ministry of Finance; Municipal Business Licence Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the Canada Revenue Agency for corporate income tax and GST/HST. If operating in British Columbia and revenues are subject to PST, register through OneStop BC. Apply for a municipal business licence for the registered office, including a mobile or home-office licence if applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA account activation is delayed, contact CRA Business Enquiries with the incorporation certificate. If municipal licensing is refused, address the stated non-compliance, resubmit, and pay any prescribed administrative penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 6201 software operations do not require an industrial licence in British Columbia; any municipal business licence is issued by the relevant city
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required as a statutory operating permit; a general municipal business licence may apply to the registered office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – software development is not a listed trigger activity under the Environmental Assessment Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste thresholds apply; e-waste and electronic component disposal must comply with BC Recycling Regulation B.C. Reg. 449/2004

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required in the absence of a physical production facility; no fire safety certification or structural load inspection is mandatory. If employees are engaged, WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and employer injury protection coverage are required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — GST/HST and Business Number registration; BC Ministry of Finance, Taxation Branch — BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) registration via eTaxBC
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada must obtain a Business Number (BN) from the CRA. Registration is available online through CRA Business Registration Online or by filing Form RC1. The entity must register for GST/HST once its worldwide taxable supplies of Canadian goods/services (including deemed supplies) exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or in a consecutive four-quarter period. A separate BC PST account must be opened with eTaxBC before the first taxable sale/lease of software or other PST-taxable goods is made in British Columbia; there is no minimum PST registration threshold. The ULC must provide its registered office address in BC, director/officer information, and Canadian withholding/agent details where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a federal check-the-box election. A BC Unlimited Liability Corporation is a separate taxable corporation under the Canadian Income Tax Act. For U.S. federal income tax purposes only, eligible U.S. owners may make an entity classification election on IRS Form 8832 to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity/pass-through; however, Canadian hybrid mismatch legislation (Income Tax Act subsection 18(f) and paragraph 12(2.2)) may apply to deny deductions or require income inclusions on certain hybrid/non-recognition transactions. No other entity-level pass-through election is available for Canadian GST/HST purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (5% federal Goods and Services Tax) and British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST; 7% separate retail sales tax on taxable software and related supplies)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 (worldwide taxable supplies threshold). BC PST: no minimum threshold; registration required before making the first taxable sale/lease in British Columbia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoicing, or digital stamping by the CRA. GST/HST tax invoices and simplified invoices must contain the prescribed information under the Excise Tax Act and Regulations. For app-store sales through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the app-store operator may issue transaction records directly to consumers; the Canadian seller must retain electronic sales reports, payment settlement records, and detailed invoices sufficient to support filed GST/HST and BC PST returns. No government API clearance is currently required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of digital property or service is zero-rated for GST/HST where the recipient is a non-resident and the supply is not received or enjoyed in Canada, and the supplier has the required evidence of the non-resident status and delivery to an address/geographic location outside Canada. For physical goods exported by the supplier, the goods must be exported as part of the sale, and the supplier must retain proof of physical export. Mobile utility app sales made through Canadian app-store channels to consumers physically located in Canada remain subject to GST/HST and, where applicable, BC PST; sales clearly made to non-residents and not enjoyed in Canada may be zero-rated if full documentary support is maintained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Customs Export Declaration (B13A Export Declaration or equivalent)
Commercial invoice or sales contract showing non-resident purchaser and foreign destination
Bill of Lading / air waybill / carrier proof of export for physical goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or FX receipt showing foreign currency settlement
App store transaction report, IP/geo-location evidence, and non-resident attestation for digital supplies
BC PST exemption and export collection documentation where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to strict CRA audit scrutiny. If evidence of export or non-resident receipt is lacking, the CRA may reassess the supply at the full 5% GST/HST rate plus arrears interest and may impose a wilful-participation penalty under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act. Knowingly issuing false or misleading export invoices or refund claims can trigger penalties of up to 25% of unreported tax plus criminal prosecution under section 239 of the Income Tax Act and comparable provincial offences. BC PST audits may also claw back uncollected/undocumented PST of 7% plus interest and penalties under the BC Provincial Sales Tax Act. Any retroactive clawback generally begins from the date of the original zero-rated filing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a current account convertibility regime with unrestricted repatriation of software export proceeds; capital account transactions require Bank of Canada approval for investments exceeding CAD 100 million per year and are subject to foreign investment review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds; digital receipts from app stores must be deposited into corporate accounts and reported to the Canada Revenue Agency under transfer pricing and income tax obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for cross-border receipt platforms such as Stripe or Wise; legal constraints include FINTRAC registration and Bank of Canada foreign exchange reporting for transactions exceeding prescribed thresholds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate onboarding is permitted through e-KYC and video verification; physical presence of directors is not mandatory but may be required for in-person verification in complex ownership or high-risk structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership non-disclosure or shell company structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry search extracts, director and shareholder identification documents, and beneficial ownership declaration compliant with FINTRAC guidelines
Due diligence search results and client source of funds documentation

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' for capital contributions; requires corporate resolution authorizing the injection and verification against registered share capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements routed via SWIFT MT103 for payments to international suppliers or app store settlements; Commercial Letters of Credit are not applicable for digital software services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor General
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation plus 2 months; due annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty CAD 100 (approx USD 75); failure to file within 2 months after anniversary triggers automatic administrative strike-off; reinstatement via court order or registrar consent with CAD 500 filing fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (includes Schedule 1 and provincial top-up)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance (provincial corporate allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the taxation year-end (standard fiscal year); for ULC with December 31 year-end, due by June 30 annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file T2: immediate 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per full month of unpaid tax (up to 12%); repeated failure: alternative penalty (10%); underlying tax interest increases via prescribed daily rates; BC provincial penalty is 0.5% per month of non-filed BC provincial allocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and Provincial Allocations Audit Confirmation (if applicable – for ULC pass-through structures)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: With T2 filing; no separate annual filing deadline, but must be consistent with T2
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misallocations trigger reassessment, interest, and administrative penalties (up to 10% of net understated amount); repeated negligence may result in gross-negligence penalty of 50% of misreported income.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory revenue or asset threshold triggers an audit for a BC unlimited liability corporation. Audit is mandatory only if the company is a 'public issuer' under BCBCA, a regulated financial institution, or if shareholders (holding at least 10% of votes) request an auditor under section 200 BCBCA. A private ULC may unanimously dispense with an audit and appoint a review engagement instead.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Part I of CPA Canada Handbook) or ASPE (Part II of CPA Canada Handbook); ULCs eligible for private enterprise reporting unless articles require otherwise.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC does not maintain a separate UBO annual filing. The annual report must confirm current directors, registered office, and corporate name. Changes in shareholding or beneficial ownership are not disclosed to BC Registry but must be recorded internally in the register of members and in minutes; if the ULC transacts with CRA, substantial presence and ultimate owners must be tracked for tax filings under section 212. BC effective control determination follows the 'controlling mind' rules under BCBCA; no annual public UBO return exists.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (with classes, series, transfers, and beneficial ownership notes)
Register of Directors (name, address, consent, council resolution)
Central Securities Register (if shares are issued in uncertificated form)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (if audit dispensed) or 4,000-12,000 (if shareholders request audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate to 9% and BC rate to 2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-Controlled Private Corporations (CCPC); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits up to 35% refundable for qualifying R&D expenditures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and BC provincial combined) filed via CRA's NETFILE or E-file system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide revenue; non-resident shareholders do not file this return, but the corporation must report all income earned in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate taxable income per Part I of the Income Tax Act; apply SBD and other deductions as applicable.
Compute combined federal and BC tax; claim foreign tax credits if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed calculation of taxable income and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach all required schedules, including T106 for transfer pricing if thresholds met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 5% per month up to 12 months (max 50% of unpaid tax); interest on unpaid amounts at prescribed rates; additional penalties for repeated failures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty rate, submit Form NR301 (or NR302 for partnerships) to CRA, provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, and ensure the beneficial owner meets treaty conditions (e.g., 5% voting shareholding for 5% rate under Canada-US treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty rate 10% (Canada-US); Interest: statutory 25%, treaty rate 15% (Canada-US, often reduced to 0% for arm's length interest).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if gross revenue ≥ CAD 50 million and cross-border related party transactions ≥ CAD 1 million (services) or ≥ CAD 5 million (other); Master File if gross revenue ≥ CAD 100 million and cross-border related party transactions ≥ CAD 5 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in offshore jurisdictions, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) applies to deny tax benefits from transactions lacking commercial substance. ULCs must maintain real economic activity and substance to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or misrepresentation of revenue in T2 filings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239; fines up to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, and civil penalties up to 50% of tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes under s.227.1; travel bans and asset freezes possible; personal bankruptcy may not discharge tax debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pass-through entity without real business activities, employees, or assets in BC; using ULC solely to avoid US tax on Canadian income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment disallowing tax benefits; penalties up to 50% of tax avoided; potential treaty shopping denial under LOB provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for corporate debts if the company is deemed a sham; courts may pierce the veil for fraudulent or improper conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a money services business (MSB) if handling virtual currency or payment processing; inadequate KYC/AML procedures for app store transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) up to CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal charges for directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined up to CAD 500,000 and imprisoned up to 5 years for willful non-compliance; civil liability for damages.
